drivingQuestion: Why does R' Akiva need 'it is a guilt offering' when tradition already teaches the substitute grazes?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is answered in the next unit (Rav Huna).

segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ כּוּ׳. הוּא קָרֵב וְאֵין תְּמוּרָתוֹ קְרֵיבָה. לְמָה לִי קְרָא, וְהָא הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לָהּ!
segments.en: § The baraita stated that in contrast to Rabbi Yishmael, «Rabbi Akiva says» that the word “only” «is unnecessary» to exclude the offspring and substitutes of other sacrificial animals from being sacrificed upon the altar, as the verse that discusses guilt offerings: “It is a guilt offering” (Leviticus 5:19), teaches that only «it,» the guilt offering itself, «is sacrificed, but its substitute is not offered.» The Gemara asks: «Why do I» need «a verse» to teach this? «Didn’t» the Sages «learn this halakha,» that the substitute of a guilt offering is left to graze, as a tradition transmitted to Moses from Sinai, since they said that in any case where a sin offering is left to die, in the parallel case involving a guilt offering, the animal is not sacrificed but rather left to graze?
